description: A percussion voice made of two naive square waves and whatever can be read from the relation between them: cross-modulation, one of five logic operators, a filter and two envelopes

params.text: Sets the pitch of the first oscillator, two octaves below to seven above C1
Sets the second oscillator as a ratio of the first, nineteen steps: twelve whole-number ratios, a unison, a unison detuned by one per cent, and four irrational ones
Skews the pulse widths, widening the first oscillator and narrowing the second together; both are square at the centre
Sets the rate the logic core runs at, from four times the host rate down to 250Hz
Divides the first oscillator by a flip-flop chain: straight through, by two, four, eight or sixteen, each division a half-duty square a subharmonic below
Sets how deeply the two oscillators modulate each other, up to four octaves
Sets which way that modulation goes: both at full depth at the centre, where the feedback is, the first modulating the second fully anticlockwise, the reverse fully clockwise
Chooses what the modulation changes: frequency, amplitude, or both
Chooses which operator reads the two oscillators, crossfading between neighbours rather than switching: and, sum, ring, flip or noise
Crossfades between the first oscillator alone and the operator's output
Sets the filter cutoff, 20Hz to 12000Hz
Sets the filter resonance, up to a ringing that lasts seconds; a trigger pings it
Chooses whether the filter is a low-pass or a band-pass
Drives the saturator that ends the chain, 0 to +24dB; it is not a volume control
Sets how long the modulation envelope takes to fall
Bends the fall of the modulation envelope, from convex through linear to concave
Sets how long the amplitude envelope takes to rise
Sets how long the amplitude envelope takes to fall, reaching exactly zero so a hit ends in silence
Bends the amplitude envelope, from convex, which is slow to leave the peak, through linear to concave, which drops away like an exponential
Sets how far the modulation envelope moves the pitch, either way
Sets how far the modulation envelope walks the relation control up or down the list of operators
Sets how far the modulation envelope moves the filter cutoff, either way
Strikes the voice by hand

inputs.text: A rising edge strikes the voice: it resets both oscillator phases, restarts the modulation envelope and pings the filter
Added to the pitch knob, one volt per octave
Added to the ratio knob, a step of the table per two volts
Added to the xmod knob, a fifth of its travel per volt; the total is held between the two ends of it
Added to the relation knob, two fifths of a step per volt
Added to the cutoff knob, one volt per octave

outputs.text: The voice taken before the amplitude envelope, through the filter and the saturator with the amplifier held open, so the module drones instead of striking
The voice, everything through the amplifier

notes: the operators are: and, the smaller of the two, high only when both are; sum, their average, three-valued; ring, their product, an exclusive-or for two bipolar squares.
the other two are flip, a latch the first oscillator sets and the second clears, and noise, an eight-bit shift register clocked by the first and fed against the second.
the engine idles when nothing is sounding, so patching the drone jack is what tells it to keep running; unpatched it costs nothing.
a trigger does everything it normally does while the drone is running, so the drone jack is the place to hear what a hit does to the sound with the amplitude envelope out of the way.
menu: Oscillator phase on trigger — Reset (repeatable hits), or Free-running (every hit differs)
Osc B phase offset — where the second oscillator starts when the phases are reset: 0 deg, 90 deg, 180 deg or 270 deg
Env 2 on retrigger — Retrigger, or Free (finish the running one)
Ratio knob — Table (19 steps), or Free (0.25x - 4x)
Cutoff tracks pitch — makes the filter follow the pitch jack
Velocity from trigger height — takes the level of the hit from how high the trigger goes
Output level — 5 Vpp, 10 Vpp or 14 Vpp

inputs.0:
high above 1V · stepped · one channel only

a negative voltage does nothing here.
inputs.1: 1V per octave · continuous · one channel only
inputs.5: 1V per octave · continuous · one channel only
